title: Daily Life - What Am I Thinking!
audio: mp3/74. Daily Life - What Am I Thinking!.mp3

segments.en: Hello English learners, welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 您好英语学习者，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: Today, we're bringing you an upper intermediate lesson and something that we all do.
segments.zh: 今天，我们为您带来一节中高级课程，讲的是我们每个人都会做的事。

segments.en: You think to yourself or you talk to yourself.
segments.zh: 你在心里想事情，或者自言自语。

segments.en: And we're going to be doing that today, but we're going to be looking at some specific vocabulary.
segments.zh: 我们今天将这样做，但我们将研究一些特定的词汇。

segments.en: Erica, why don't you tell us about that?
Well, unfortunately, we're going to be following a guy as he's in a really embarrassing situation and we're going to hear him call himself some bad names in his mind.
segments.zh: 好吧，很不巧，我们要跟着一个家伙，看他经历一个非常尴尬的处境，我们会听到他在心里骂自己。

segments.en: So he's a little bit nervous and he thinks he is not very smart, right?
segments.zh: 所以他有点紧张，他认为他不是很聪明，对吧？

segments.en: Okay, so before we start with this dialogue, there are a couple of words that we should look at in vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 好的，在开始这段对话之前，我们应该先在词汇预览里看几个词。

segments.en: All right, we're going to hear both of these words in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们将在对话中听到这两个词。

segments.en: And the first one is famished.
Okay, so famished is an adjective.
segments.zh: 好吧，Famished 是一个形容词。

segments.en: That's right, meaning very, very, very hungry.
segments.zh: 没错，意思是非常、非常、非常饿。

segments.en: Okay, so just very hungry, very easy.
segments.zh: 好吧，就是非常饿，很简单。

segments.en: Now, what about our next one?
Another adjective to describe a person, right?
segments.zh: 另一个形容一个人的形容词，对吧？

segments.en: Okay, so a sexist person would be?
segments.zh: 好吧，那什么样的人算性别歧视者呢？

segments.en: Somebody who judges people by their sex.
segments.zh: 凭性别来判断别人的人。

segments.en: So like all women are stupid, for example.
segments.zh: 比如，认为所有女人都很蠢。

segments.en: Which is not true, of course.

segments.zh: 所以性别歧视对男女都适用。

segments.en: A woman can be sexist, a man could be sexist.
segments.zh: 女人可能性别歧视，男人也可能性别歧视。

segments.en: Meaning the women thinks all men are stupid.
segments.zh: 意思是女人认为所有男人都很蠢。

segments.en: Let's just be clear about that.
So now that we've taken a look at these two phrases, let's start with our dialogue and we'll be back to talk about all the great words.
segments.zh: 现在我们看了这两个词，让我们开始听对话，之后我们会回来聊聊这些好用的词。

segments.en: I can't believe she's on a date with me.
segments.zh: 我不敢相信她和我约会。

segments.en: I must be the luckiest guy in the world.
segments.zh: 我一定是世界上最幸运的人。

segments.en: I want to scream at the top of my lungs.
I'm the luckiest dude in the world.
segments.zh: 我是世界上最幸运的人。
她让我都变得性别歧视了。

segments.en: Oh, right, I have a salad. Oh, crap!
segments.zh: 哦，对了，我也有沙拉。哦，糟了！

segments.en: She's going to think I'm a moron.
What the hell are all these forks for?
segments.zh: 这些叉子到底都是干什么用的？

segments.en: Okay, chill, be cool, be cool. Just take a fork. Eat your salad. Um... Mm? Sorry, you were saying?
segments.zh: 好吧，冷静，冷静，冷静。 拿一个叉子就行。 吃你的沙拉。 嗯……嗯？ 对不起，你刚才说什么？
好吧，第一次约会很尴尬，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, I mean I really do feel sorry for this guy.
segments.zh: 是的，我的意思是我真的为这个人感到难过。

segments.en: Sometimes we are in the company of a very beautiful girl and we just get really nervous.
segments.zh: 有时我们和一个非常漂亮的女孩在一起，我们真的很紧张。

segments.en: Alright, well, you know, psychologists call this negative self-talk.
segments.zh: 好吧，好吧，你知道，心理学家称之为负面的自我对话。

segments.en: Yeah, this sort of calling yourself names and talking negatively about yourself.
segments.zh: 是的，就是这种骂自己、说自己坏话的行为。

segments.en: But actually you can use some of this language to talk negatively about others.
segments.zh: 但实际上你可以使用这种语言中的一些来消极地谈论其他人。

segments.en: So why don't we look now at this language in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不现在在语言要点中看看这种语言。

segments.en: So on Language Takeaway today we have five words.
segments.zh: 所以今天的语言要点我们有五个词。

segments.en: Let's start with our first one.
segments.zh: 让我们从我们的第一个开始。

segments.en: Okay, now this isn't a very polite word I would say.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在这不是我会说的一个非常礼貌的词。

segments.en: Okay, but what is a dumbass?
Well, it's obviously a dumb, stupid idiot.
segments.zh: 好吧，显然就是指又笨又蠢的笨蛋。

segments.en: Okay, so it's a person that is not very intelligent.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是一个不是很聪明的人。

segments.en: And our next word is also quite similar.
segments.zh: 我们的下一个词也很相似。

segments.en: If a person is a dumbass or a person is a moron, what's the difference?
segments.zh: 如果一个人是个笨蛋或一个人是白痴，那有什么区别？

segments.en: Well, basically a moron is someone who is not smart, who is very unintelligent.
segments.zh: 好吧，基本上，白痴是不聪明的人，非常不聪明。

segments.en: So they don't know what one plus one is.
segments.zh: 所以他们不知道一加一是什么。

segments.en: But a dumbass is a person who does stupid things.
segments.zh: 但笨蛋是一个做愚蠢事情的人。

segments.en: So maybe a dumbass like you're planning a bank robbery and the dumbass forgets to bring the gun.
segments.zh: 所以，dumbass 可能是这样：你策划抢银行，结果那个笨蛋忘了带枪。

segments.en: So maybe moron is a little bit less offensive and it's actually you'll find it in the dictionary, right?
segments.zh: 所以 moron 可能没那么冒犯，其实你在字典里能找到这个词，对吧？

segments.en: Whereas a dumbass I don't think you'll find it.
segments.zh: 而我不认为你会找到它。

segments.en: It's also a negative name you can call people.
segments.zh: 这也是一个负面的名字，你可以叫人。

segments.en: This is very strange because I don't know how a tool can be something negative towards a person.
segments.zh: 这很奇怪，因为我不明白'工具'怎么会是形容人的贬义词。

segments.en: But it actually means the opposite, right?
segments.zh: 但其实它的意思正好相反，对吧？

segments.en: If a person is called a tool, it means they are useless, right?
segments.zh: 如果一个人被叫做 tool，意思是说他没用，对吧？

segments.en: So if you ever call the tool, they're saying that you're useless.
segments.zh: 所以如果有人叫你 tool，就是在说你没用。

segments.en: Well, these are three interesting words.
So why don't we hear some examples of each of these words in use?
segments.zh: 那么为什么我们没有听到使用中每个词的一些例子呢？

segments.en: Last week he borrowed my mobile phone and dropped it in the pool.
segments.zh: 上周他借了我的手机，结果掉进了游泳池里。

segments.en: I don't like Kevin very much.
He can be a real moron at times.
segments.zh: 他有时可能是一个真正的白痴。

segments.en: It was looking for a joke, but he didn't even have a resume prepared.
segments.zh: 他在找笑话，但他连简历都没准备。

segments.en: Okay, so great examples and here at EnglishPod, we're bringing you real street talk.
segments.zh: 好的，很好的例子，在 Englishpod，我们为您带来真正的街头谈话。

segments.en: Language as it is spoken by today's youth.
segments.zh: 今天的年轻人说的语言。

segments.en: Now let's take a look at our last two words.
segments.zh: 现在让我们来看看我们最后两个字。

segments.en: Well, these phrases you can use when you're trying to calm yourself down and make yourself relax a little bit, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，当您试图让自己平静下来并让自己放松一点时，您可以使用这些短语，对吧？

segments.en: Let's take a look at the next one.
And then you also need to be cool.
segments.zh: 然后你还需要保持冷静。

segments.en: Now if you can tell the pattern is related to temperature, right?
segments.zh: 现在如果你能看出模式与温度有关，对吧？

segments.en: So again, that's what it means to relax.
segments.zh: 再说一次，这就是放松的意义。

segments.en: Make your emotions not so hot.
segments.zh: 让你的情绪别那么激动。

segments.en: And you use them together like that, don't you?
segments.zh: 你就这样一起使用它们，不是吗？

segments.en: Now chill also has another way of using it, right?
segments.zh: 现在 Chill 还有另一种使用方式，对吧？
我和朋友们一起放松呢。

segments.en: We're chilling here in the EnglishPod studio.
segments.zh: 我们正在 EnglishPod 工作室里放松呢。
这意味着我们只是在放松。

segments.en: You have to drop the G. Yeah.
segments.zh: 你得把 G 省掉。对。

segments.en: You have to say I'm chilling.
So that's all for language takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以这就是语言要点的全部内容。

segments.en: But now let's take a look at some of the really useful phrases that we saw in this dialogue in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 但现在让我们来看看这段对话里出现的一些非常实用的短语，进入流利表达。

segments.en: So this guy is so happy he's on this date that he wants to scream at the top of his lungs.
segments.zh: 这家伙因为这次约会太开心了，开心得想扯着嗓子大喊。

segments.en: Scream at the top of my lungs.
Scream at the top of my lungs.
So basically he just wants to scream.
segments.zh: 所以基本上他只是想尖叫。

segments.en: So for example, sometimes you're at a concert, right?
segments.zh: 例如，有时你在音乐会上，对吧？

segments.en: And you need to talk to your friend and you're screaming at the top of your lungs because the other person can't hear you.
segments.zh: 你要跟朋友说话，就得扯着嗓子大喊，因为对方听不到你。

segments.en: So you're lost in the woods and you need to scream at the top of your lungs so that someone will hear you and find you.
segments.zh: 比如你在树林里迷路了，你得扯着嗓子大喊，这样才有人能听到你、找到你。

segments.en: So scream at the top of my lungs.
segments.zh: 所以就是 scream at the top of my lungs，扯着嗓子大喊。

segments.en: So if I tell you, Erica, you need to get it together.
segments.zh: 所以如果我说，Erica，你需要振作起来。

segments.en: Basically you're telling me to calm down, relax.
segments.zh: 基本上你是在告诉我冷静下来，放松一下。

segments.en: So pull your emotions together, get your ideas straight.
segments.zh: 就是把情绪收一收，把思路理清楚。

segments.en: So it kind of gives you this idea that you got to pull, like you said, pull your emotions together in a little box and tie them up.
segments.zh: 所以它给人的感觉是，就像你说的，要把情绪收进一个小盒子里，捆起来。

segments.en: So Marco, when would you use this phrase, get it together?
segments.zh: 那么 Marco，你什么时候会用 get it together 这个短语？

segments.en: I guess when somebody is either very emotional, maybe crying or very nervous, you tell the person, oh, get it together, relax.
segments.zh: 我想，当有人情绪很激动，可能在哭，或者非常紧张时，你会对那个人说，哦，振作起来，放松点。

segments.en: Or when somebody maybe is not doing something good in their life, like making bad decisions or not being responsible, you tell that person, you need to get it together.
segments.zh: 或者当某人在生活中做得不好时，比如做错决定、不负责任，你就会对那个人说，你需要振作起来。

segments.en: I couldn't have said it better myself.
segments.zh: 我自己说得再好不过了。

segments.en: So now why don't we move on to our next phrase?
segments.zh: 那么现在我们为什么不继续我们的下一个短语呢？

segments.en: And this is really, really high frequency.
segments.zh: 这个使用频率真的非常非常高。

segments.en: I think you would hear it all the time.
So why would you say what the hell?
segments.zh: 那你为什么要说什么鬼？

segments.en: Well, obviously you're asking a question, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，显然你在问一个问题，对吧？

segments.en: Because you got your W, you got your what.
segments.zh: 因为里面有 W，也就是 what 的 W。

segments.en: But when you say the hell, you're putting emphasis on the what.
segments.zh: 但当你说 the hell 时，是在给 what 加强语气。

segments.en: So you're asking a really strong question.
segments.zh: 所以你在问一个非常强烈的问题。

segments.en: So if I say what the hell is going on?
segments.zh: 所以如果我说到底发生了什么？

segments.en: So, and we can change it a little bit.
segments.zh: 所以，我们可以稍微改变一下。

segments.en: We can replace the what with another WH like why, how, where, where or when.
segments.zh: 我们可以把 what 换成其他的 WH 词，比如 why、how、where 或 when。

segments.en: So why don't we hear some examples of how this expression is used using different WH words?
segments.zh: 那我们为什么不听几个例子，看看这个表达用不同的 WH 词怎么用呢？

segments.en: Example one, where the hell are you?

segments.zh: 我已经等了好几个小时了。

segments.en: Example two, how the hell did you do that?
segments.zh: 示例二，你到底是怎么做到的？

segments.en: Example three, when the hell are you going to find a job?
segments.zh: 例子三，你到底打算什么时候找工作？

segments.en: I'm tired of paying for everything.
segments.zh: 我厌倦了为一切付出代价。

segments.en: Example four, who the hell are you?
Now our final word, also a little bit strong, but pretty high frequency.
segments.zh: 现在看最后一个词，语气也有点重，但使用频率相当高。

segments.en: So it's a little bit strong, but less strong than maybe saying a really bad word.
segments.zh: 所以它的语气有点重，但没有说那种真正的脏话那么重。

segments.en: But it's definitely saying like you made a mistake.
segments.zh: 但它肯定是在说你犯了一个错误。

segments.en: It's like a really strong, oh no.
segments.zh: 它就像语气很重的'哦，不'。

segments.en: But I guess not many people say, oh no.
segments.zh: 但我想在那种情况下没多少人会说'哦，不'。
我刚刚损失了 1000 万美元。

segments.en: So it's a very strong, oh no, but it's not as strong as it could be.
segments.zh: 所以它是一个语气很重的'哦，不'，但还不是最重的。

segments.en: There are other words out there that are stronger, but we are not going to go into them here.
segments.zh: 还有别的词语气更重，但我们这里就不细说了。

segments.en: But maybe you guys know, so let us know.
segments.zh: 但也许你们知道，所以让我们知道。

segments.en: We can definitely keep an eye out on the comment section.
segments.zh: 我们一定会留意评论区的。

segments.en: But don't write the words in the comment section.
segments.zh: 但不要在评论部分写下单词。

segments.en: So we saw some really great phrases, some really great words, a lot of informal language, but it's very high frequency and you'll use that with your friends or you'll see it in movies, TV shows.
segments.zh: 所以我们学了一些很棒的短语和词，很多非正式用语，但使用频率非常高，你会跟朋友用，或者在电影、电视节目里看到。

segments.en: Really common in movies and TV shows.
segments.zh: 在电影和电视节目中确实很常见。

segments.en: So let's listen to this dialogue one more time and then we'll come back and talk a little bit more.
segments.zh: 所以让我们再听一次这个对话，然后我们会回来再谈一点。

segments.en: I can't believe she's on a date with me.
segments.zh: 我不敢相信她和我约会。

segments.en: I must be the luckiest guy in the world.
segments.zh: 我一定是世界上最幸运的人。

segments.en: I want to scream at the top of my lungs, 'I'm the luckiest dude in the world!'
segments.zh: 我真想扯着嗓子大喊：“我是全世界最幸运的家伙！”

segments.en: She's so hot. She's making me sexist.
segments.zh: 她太迷人了，害我都说出这种性别歧视的话。

segments.en: Oh crap, which fork do I use?
Damn it! She's gonna think I'm a moron.
segments.zh: 该死！她会认为我是个白痴。

segments.en: What the hell are all these forks for?
segments.zh: 这些叉子到底都是干什么用的？

segments.en: So these slang words, they're actually very common, right?
segments.zh: 所以这些俚语，它们实际上很常见，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, I think like you said, it's not likely that you'll find them in a dictionary.
segments.zh: 是的，我想就像你说的，你不太可能在字典中找到它们。

segments.en: Of course. And you can find them in movies, or sometimes when you're having a conversation, a very informal conversation with a native speaker, these words will slip out and these slang terms will come up.
segments.zh: 当然。 你可以在电影里找到它们，或者有时你跟母语人士进行非常随意的谈话时，这些词会脱口而出，这些俚语就会冒出来。

segments.en: There's a great resource out there for wonderful English slang terms, called UrbanDictionary.com.
segments.zh: 有一个查询英语俚语的好资源，叫 UrbanDictionary.com。

segments.en: Exactly. If you ever see a word that maybe you can't find in the conventional dictionary, you're probably gonna find it there.
segments.zh: 没错。 如果你在传统词典中看到一个可能找不到的单词，你可能会在那里找到它。

segments.en: Yeah, we'll put a link up to it on the site.
segments.zh: 是的，我们会在网站上放置一个链接。

segments.en: Alright. So also, if you have any questions or comments, be sure to come to our website, EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 好的。 同样，如果您有任何问题或意见，请务必访问我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.en: Marco and I are there to answer all your questions, and we also got lots of resources, like links to Urban Dictionary.
segments.zh: Marco 和我在那里回答你所有的问题，我们也有很多资源，比如城市词典的链接。

segments.en: Right. And also, if you have any questions on any other slang terms that you may have heard, or how to use them, be sure to post it on the comment section.
segments.zh: 对。 此外，如果您对您可能听说过的任何其他俚语或如何使用它们有任何疑问，请务必将其发布在评论部分。

segments.en: Well guys, thanks for listening to this lesson, and until next time, goodbye!
segments.zh: 好吧，伙计们，感谢收听本课，下次再见！
